features.method: The eight strings of cluster 1 (one central, seven on a heptagon of 60 m radius), centre string +203 m east and +271 m north of the pattern centroid. Layout: the eight string positions of each cluster are the eight dark-green dots of that cluster in the top view (Fig. 1, right panel) of arXiv:2309.16310 (ICRC 2023), a to-scale schematic with a north arrow and a 0-100 m bar. Detected by colour (97 dots), the schematic was registered by a similarity transform onto the measured planar positions of the strings of clusters 1 to 8 plotted in Fig. 2 of arXiv:2108.00212 (axes in metres, "X is eastbound, Y is northbound"): 63 of the 64 dots of clusters 1 to 8 match a measured string within 8 m (rms 3.1 m), scale 2.58 m per pixel, rotation 0.1 deg. Clusters 1 to 11 have 8 dots each (one spurious detection at cluster 5 removed); clusters 12 and 13 are drawn incomplete in that figure (5 and 2 or 3 dots) and clusters 14 to 16 have no top view, so they are not drawn. Within a cluster the seven outer strings lie 58 m to 62 m from the central one (stated: "a regular heptagon with the radius of 60 m"). The schematic is idealised and the measured 2021 positions scatter by up to about 6 m about the ideal heptagon, so strings are good to about 5 m relative to each other. The two source frames have no stated origin. Placement: the centroid of the eleven central strings is put at the published site coordinate, 51 46' N, 104 24' E (arXiv:2309.16310, 2412.00164, 2507.01893; rounded to a minute), in an azimuthal-equidistant projection (WGS 84) with the figure's north up. That coordinate is not defined as a cluster, so the pattern as a whole is only good to about 1500 m: a minute of latitude is 1.85 km, a minute of longitude 1.15 km, the point could be any cluster or the field centre, and a 2013 paper gives 51 50' N, 104 20' E, 8.7 km away. Each string is a 1 m square position marker (a string anchor on the lakebed is a few metres across at most; size symbolic).

map.name: Baikal-GVD: clusters of strings in southern Lake Baikal

summary.plain: The Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope in southern Lake Baikal: eleven clusters of eight light-sensor strings each on the lake bed, drawn at their published layout and deployment year. The pattern is accurate to a few metres internally, but its place on the lake is only known to about a kilometre and a half.
